ownership_reason: Only the gold iterates the collection and sees each element together with the list as it stands at that moment, after the earlier elements of the same call have gone in, and only the gold decides whether an element takes a slot of the run; hops 1-4 pass the receiver, the index and the whole collection along unchanged and get back nothing but the change in size, and once an element has been placed one slot too far no caller can tell which slot was skipped. The gold's javadoc promises the elements inserted as one run that begins at the given index; on the trigger the run [4] begins at index 1. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('Only elements that are not already in this list will be added, and duplicates from the specified collection will be ignored'); ListOrderedSet.addAll(int, Collection), production code doing the same step (a contained element is skipped and the index moves on only after an insertion), with TestListOrderedSet testListAddIndexed ([3, 0, 2] added at 1 to [0, 1] gives [0, 3, 2, 1]); SetUniqueList.add(int, Object), the receiver's refusal of a contained element, with TestSetUniqueList testListIterator; SetUniqueList.decorate, the production caller ('If the list contains duplicates, these are removed (first indexed one kept)'), with TestSetUniqueList testFactory and testAddAll. A hop that removes the receiver's refusals before the gold must predict them outside the receiver, a second implementation of SetUniqueList's uniqueness rule by equals and hashCode that agrees with the receiver only when its set does; a hop that inserts through the receiver's list iterator replaces the gold's loop altogether.
